description: Whether a body paragraph of the translated document opens with a first line indent. Until now nobody decided this: the paragraph finder reads the answer off the source geometry, paragraph by paragraph, by asking whether the first line's first character sits more than a point to the right of the paragraph box, and the typesetting stage acts on that answer by moving the pen four space widths in. That is a faithful reproduction of the source and it is not a typographic policy, because the two languages do not share one. English magazine setting commonly runs the first paragraph of a section flush and indents the rest, and it also runs whole articles flush with space between paragraphs; Chinese convention indents every paragraph, first included. Reproducing the source therefore lands a Chinese page on an English convention, one paragraph at a time, with no place to say otherwise. indent_mode is that place. source leaves every paragraph exactly as the geometry said, which is what every run before this pass existed did. all indents every body paragraph. none indents none. all_but_first indents every body paragraph except the one that opens its article, which is the English convention stated as a rule rather than inferred from a box. indent_mode_by_target selects one of them by the run's target language, matched by the longest declared prefix of the language tag, as the standing translation instruction selects its role text, so a rule stated for a language holds for every variety of it; a target language no entry claims falls back to source, which is the behaviour that existed before, because a layout policy guessed for an unnamed language is worse than no policy. body_labels is the closed set of layout labels this pass may touch. It holds the labels that name running body text and nothing else: a title, a caption, a table of contents record and a masthead list are all set to their own rules and an indent decided for body text is wrong for each of them, so they are left with whatever the source geometry said. Membership of an article is a further condition, and it is a structural fact rather than a setting, so nothing here turns it on or off: a paragraph is indented only where the canonical article grouping claimed it as part of some article, asked per paragraph rather than per page. A page belonging to a feature does not make an advertisement block sharing that page part of the feature, and a page whose classification fell back to the default type is not an article merely by landing there. A paragraph no article holds is recorded under outside_article and set flush. article_opening_rank is which paragraph of an article all_but_first treats as the first one, counted over body labelled paragraphs in document order within the article, which is the same rank the drop cap pass counts. indent_em is the amount an indent moves the pen, in half widths of a space, and it is a pin rather than a control: the amount lives in the typesetting stage as a multiplier and this pass decides only whether a paragraph is indented, not by how much. It is declared here so that the number is written down in one readable place and so that a gate can hold the stage to it; changing it here alone would make this file describe a page it does not produce. functional_clearance_pt is the margin, in page points, added past a measured functional avoidance: where the source's first line stepped aside for an ornament or a piece of artwork, the restored indent is the measured step plus this margin, so the translated line clears the ink it clears rather than grazing it. It bounds only that restoration; the stylistic indent stays the em multiple the typesetting stage has always used.

indent_mode_by_target.description: One mode per target language, keyed by language tag. zh is declared all because Chinese convention indents every paragraph including the first. No other language is declared, so every other run falls back to source and is laid out exactly as it was before this pass existed.
